text.unicode: LF match byte+1 and text.len are valid UTF-8 boundaries. Borrowed changed_old/new are trimmed at shared scalar boundaries and correspond to changed_a/b. Valid UTF-8 string equality is equivalent to scalar-slice equality, preserving line token IDs and Histogram input order.
text.line_boundaries: Group is at least one. Empty input yields [0], exact group/terminal LF avoids duplicate end, partial final groups and CRLF preserve previous LF grouping semantics.
text.ordered_cursors: Locked HunkIter documentation and implementation guarantee monotonic disjoint before and after ranges. Each cursor counts the gap from previous end to next start, then the changed range, so byte slices never reverse and cumulative counts recover the original scalar offsets.
text.zero_extent_hunks: Pure insertion or deletion uses an empty slice and zero added scalar count on the unchanged side. Cursors remain at the same byte boundary until the subsequent ordered hunk; a wholly empty document has the required boundary index zero.
text.capacity_and_errors: Existing checked combined scalar capacity limit, character refinement and UTF-16 rendering are unchanged. No new public API, recoverable Error branch or reordered existing Error is introduced.
text.space_claim: Boundary vectors contain one usize per boundary, with four stack usize cursor counters. No measured heap or timing improvement is asserted by this review.

rfc_tail.original_length: Captured at line 720 before any patch mutation. The parents-empty early return cannot have retained capacity due to this rationalize invocation because no mutation occurred.
rfc_tail.condition: At lines 920-924, shrink_to_fit is requested once only if final operation count is below the initial operation count. Successful contents, operation order and payload representation are unaffected.
rfc_tail.error_contract: The call is after all fallible rationalization logic and before Ok. Existing Error results and their priority are unchanged. Like existing allocation operations, allocation failure is not converted to a new recoverable Error.
rfc_tail.capacity: Vec::shrink_to_fit is a capacity reduction request, not a promise of capacity==len. It may reallocate; no measured peak-memory or timing claim is asserted.

production_observed.freeze_note: Parent confirmed this frozen source after completing its validation. This reviewer independently verified only the source hash; no compilation, tests, benchmarks or other validation was rerun.

proof.lane_isolation: Each byte lane of different&0x7f is in [0,127]; adding the corresponding 0x7f lane gives [127,254]. No carry crosses the byte boundary, including the most significant lane. The wrapping_add does not introduce an inter-lane effect.
proof.exact_zero: For a lane d, the sum high bit is zero iff (d&0x7f)==0. OR with original d excludes d==0x80, and OR with LOW clears all lower output bits after complement. The final HIGH mask has a set lane iff d==0, precisely source_byte==0x0a. Non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes, including 0x8a continuation bytes, cannot become false LF hits.
proof.endianness_and_order: from_le_bytes puts source byte i in lane i independent of host endianness. Mask bits are at 8*i+7, so trailing_zeros()/8 recovers i. Clearing the least significant set bit iterates all hits in increasing source order; outer chunks enumerate in increasing order.
proof.bounds: block*8+i denotes a byte inside a complete chunk, so newline_at byte+1 is <=text.len(). remainder_start=text.len()-remainder.len() is exactly the first unscanned byte; all residual bytes are examined once in ascending order. Empty input, a length divisible by eight and tails of one through seven bytes are all covered.
proof.group_semantics: The unchanged closure increments once per actual LF, emits just after each group-th LF and resets its count. The caller supplies group>=1 using ceil((LF_count+2)/(MAX_DIFF_TOKENS-1)). Terminal LF does not duplicate text.len(); an unfinished group emits the same final boundary as the previous match_indices implementation.
proof.unicode_and_errors: LF is one ASCII UTF-8 byte and cannot be inside a multibyte scalar, so emitted byte+1 is a valid scalar boundary. CRLF still counts LF only. No unsafe, public API, additional Error branch or existing error-order change is introduced.
